Title: You can only pick seats on step 2
Notes: Step 1 (Passenger Info) exposes no Select Seat control and no Seat Selection section; seats appear only after advancing to Ancillaries.

Title: You cannot reach the seats without choosing a fare package
Notes: Air Cairo has no in-wizard bundle step at all (fare package is chosen at search, before Passenger Info) - there is nothing for this case to gate on. Not scored as a failure.

Title: Missing passenger details and a missing fare package are both reported
Notes: Compound case: the missing-passenger-details half was directly confirmed reported (8 Required markers). The missing-fare-package half cannot occur on this supplier (no such wizard step, same structural reason as TC-SM-NAV-002), so the case as a whole is recorded N/A - final, most-informed verdict supersedes the earlier partial Passed reading.

Title: 'Select Seat' opens the seat map
Notes: 0 seat elements before the click; 169 after clicking Select Seat, with the traveller picker open.

Title: You can skip seats completely
Notes: Continue without seats closed the map with no seat assigned; total stayed at the base fare; Book remained enabled.

Title: The seat total matches the seats you can see
Notes: Rail SEATS count matched the actual data-seat-id count exactly on every flight checked (170/169 on SM475, 163 on SM477).

Title: Every seat has one clear state and one seat number
Notes: 170 rendered, 170 unique seat numbers, 0 duplicates; every seat resolves to exactly one state.

Title: Every seat has a full description
Notes: All 163 labels on SM477 carried seat number, row, side and cabin; zero incomplete descriptions.

Title: Cabin and section information agrees with the map
Notes: Rail and decoded cabin info agree (CABINS Economy), matching the map's own all-Economy structure.

Title: The flight shown on the map is the flight you chose
Notes: Rail flight card (SM477, departs/arrives, seats) matched the flight actually selected from search.

Title: Two different flights give two different maps
Notes: Different flights/aircraft (SM475 170 seats, SM477 163, SM478 179) each gave a distinct, matching map - never the same map reused for a different flight.

Title: Each flight in a trip gets its own map
Notes: Same evidence as RND-007: four different maps (170/169/163/179 seats) across two aircraft/flight numbers on this supplier, each matching its own rail.

Title: A taken seat can be looked at but not booked
Notes: Recorded Not Executed as written in the results doc: on this supplier a genuinely sold seat is removed from the map entirely rather than shown disabled/viewable, so the case's own precondition (taken-but-still-viewable) never occurs on this supplier's data model. Not a defect - a different, internally consistent design choice.

Title: Seat features use known wording
Notes: Only three known feature words appear across the whole map (Chargeable Seat, Leg space seat, Window seat); no unrecognised wording.

Title: Window and aisle labels match where the seat really is
Notes: Every seat in columns A/F marked Window seat, none outside those columns; zero mismatches on 163 seats.

Title: Emergency exit seats are marked
Notes: 12 exit-row seats correctly labelled Exit or emergency exit seat; each also carries its own explicit Seat not allowed for infant metadata flag.

Title: One click only shows the seat - it does not book it
Notes: Clicking a free seat opened its detail panel without incrementing the seat counter; nothing booked by the click alone.

Title: A seat is only taken when you press the button in the box
Notes: Detail panel's Book seat for name action is the only thing that assigns the seat; the click alone does not.

Title: The seat information box is correct
Notes: Clicked seat's detail-panel text was byte-identical to its own map aria-label.

Title: The bottom button changes as seats are chosen
Notes: Footer button progressed Confirm 1 of 3 seats -> Confirm 2 of 3 seats as assignments were made.

Title: Moving a passenger to another seat frees the first seat
Notes: Moving a passenger's seat released the old seat (back to available) and attached the new one, price following the move; no phantom second seat.

Title: 'Clear all seats' also removes the seat charge
Notes: Clear all seats returned both seats to available, counter to 0/3, and removed the Seat Selection line and Ancillaries and SSR subtotal entirely; no orphaned charge.

Title: Confirming saves the seat and closes the map
Notes: Confirm seat closed the map and the seat persisted into the fare breakdown.

Title: 'Change Seats' reopens the map with your choice still there
Notes: Reopening the seat control (Seat 1 more / Change Seats) restored prior assignments and the traveller counter intact.

Title: A seat held by another passenger in your booking is marked
Notes: A seat held by another passenger in the same booking is marked selected for name and carries seat--selected-other, visibly distinct from available/own-seat.

Title: The seat goes to the passenger who is selected
Notes: The seat's Book button named the active passenger explicitly; the seat attached to that passenger alone.

Title: Two passengers cannot have the same seat
Notes: With a different passenger active, clicking a seat already held by another passenger offered no Book button; counter stayed unchanged.

Title: Seats on one flight do not affect the other flight
Notes: Seats on the onward flight left the return map's counter and seats completely untouched; each journey's map is independent.

Title: Some passengers can have seats and others none
Notes: Confirmed with 2 of 3 seated: booking proceeded without complaint and the seat charge counted only the seats that existed.

Title: A seat marked 'Chargeable seat' must always have a price
Notes: All 170 seats marked Chargeable Seat also carried a real price; none rendered free. The flynas free-chargeable-seat-under-Plus defect does not reproduce (no bundles on this supplier).

Title: A paid seat is added as its own line in the price
Notes: A paid seat appears as its own Seat Selection fare line, nested under the ancillaries subtotal rather than folded into the base fare.

Title: One aircraft can have several seat prices at once
Notes: One aircraft carried three simultaneous seat price tiers (EGP 236/614/1,180); rail's from EGP 236 agreed with the cheapest.

Title: The price breakdown adds up
Notes: Base + ancillaries + tax reconciled exactly to the displayed (ceiling-rounded) total on one-way, multi-passenger and round-trip bookings alike.

Title: Gender comes from the title and cannot be edited
Notes: Gender field is disabled and derives from Title (Mr->Male, Ms->Female) on every passenger checked; cannot be set independently.

Title: Seats survive going back a step
Notes: On its own terms (navigating back/forward without editing any field), the seat summary and total were byte-identical before and after. The stronger check - actually editing a name - was then run separately and fails; see TC-SM-CNF-018.

Title: Seats, meals and bags all work together
Notes: Seat, meal and baggage lines all coexisted correctly in one booking; none overwrote another and the arithmetic was exact.

Title: What happens when the time limit runs out
Notes: The real expiry needs a genuine wall-clock wait (staging enforces 60 minutes); the countdown mechanism itself was observed working repeatedly, but the expiry-then-redirect behaviour at zero was not exercised. Same disposition as run-006 on flynas.

Title: The seat appears on the payment summary
Notes: Net Payable on the payment panel matched the fare breakdown's unrounded total exactly, including the seat charge.

Title: Clicking quickly does not book two seats
Notes: A rapid double/five-click on an available seat resulted in exactly one Book control and one assignment; no duplicate or race condition.

Title: Opening the booking page with a broken or missing link
Notes: A broken or missing flight-token produced a clean No Data Found state with Go Back/Go Home actions; no crash page or leaked internals.

Title: The seat map works on a smaller screen
Notes: At phone width (390x844) there was no horizontal page scroll and all seats still rendered; the layout reflows rather than overflowing.

Title: Seat states can be read by screen readers
Notes: Every seat is a real button whose aria-label conveys seat number, row, side, cabin, features, state and price; nothing relies on colour alone.

Title: Infants get no seat and no extras; children get both
Notes: Only the adults and the child get ancillary sections (meal/baggage); the infant has none at all and is excluded from the seat traveller picker.

Title: An infant must be linked to an adult
Notes: The infant's Assigned to field is marked required and blocks advancing to Ancillaries until set.

Title: The map moves on to the next passenger automatically
Notes: After assigning a seat, the traveller picker automatically advanced to the next unseated passenger.

Title: Each passenger type is priced separately
Notes: Each passenger type (adult/child/infant) carried its own separate base-fare and tax line; infant charged base fare + tax, not carried free.

Title: Closed passenger sections still report missing information
Failed Step: Type into a collapsed passenger section; open two sections; press Next on an incomplete collapsed passenger.
Notes: Multiple sub-checks failed: a collapsed passenger section's First Name field remained genuinely editable; two accordion sections could be open simultaneously; and an incomplete-but-collapsed passenger blocked Next with no visible signal on the collapsed header (no badge/error count) - only correct behaviour was that Next itself is blocked and Expand All resurfaces the Required markers.

Title: A changed price is shown before the booking screen
Notes: Price-mismatch trigger (fareMismatch true) could not be reproduced on Air Cairo across four separate searches/dates/fare classes; every decoded flight-token carried fareMismatch false. Not a defect - data/supplier-driven precondition never occurred this session.

Title: Accepting the new price carries it forward
Notes: Same precondition gap as TC-SM-FRC-001 - no changed-price dialog was ever produced to accept.

Title: Cancelling leaves nothing behind
Notes: Same precondition gap as TC-SM-FRC-001 - nothing to cancel out of.

Title: Every later total uses the accepted price
Notes: Same precondition gap as TC-SM-FRC-001 - no accepted-price figure existed to trace downstream.

Title: A server failure must not look like 'No Flights Found'
Notes: Not attempted or discussed anywhere in this run's results - a genuine coverage gap for this supplier pass, distinct from the documented Not-Executed groups above.

Title: The session ending in the middle of a booking
Notes: Not attempted or discussed anywhere in this run's results - a genuine coverage gap for this supplier pass.

Title: Typing in one dropdown must not affect another
Notes: A Nationality-dropdown filter typed for one passenger did not bleed into the next passenger's dropdown, which opened empty with the full country list - the sheet's previously documented defect does not reproduce on this supplier.

Title: Each offer says which airline connection it came from
Notes: All 5 result cards for the search carried the connection label, one per card, none missing.

Title: An adult travelling alone CAN take an exit seat
Notes: No exit-row seats existed on the flight (SM477) this case was first attempted on. It was not independently retried by a completed Hold/Book on the later SM475 exit-row flight the way EXR-002/003 were, though the UI check there showed an unrestricted adult's exit seat as available (indirect, not conclusive support).

Title: An adult with an infant CANNOT take an exit seat
Notes: Final verdict after a real Hold attempt with the document-number confound removed: an infant-holding adult seated in an exit row was genuinely rejected by the supplier (SPECIFIC SEAT REQUESTED NOT AVAILABLE - RESTRICTED). The rule is enforced at Hold/Book, even though the seat map itself never blocks or re-flags the selection on screen.

Title: A child CANNOT take an exit seat
Notes: Final verdict: a child seated in the same exit row was rejected by an identical real Hold failure message, mirroring EXR-002.

Title: The rule is rechecked when you switch passenger
Failed Step: Switch the active passenger while an exit-row seat's detail panel is open and compare its displayed state.
Reproducibility: Always, on every passenger switch tried
Notes: Distinct from EXR-002/003 (whether the rule is enforced at all): this case is specifically about whether the seat map's displayed state changes per passenger/per infant-assignment. It was directly and conclusively observed to never change (identical aria-label regardless of which passenger or infant-assignment is active) - a UI defect finding, not a re-statement of EXR-002/003.

Title: The rule follows the infant's linked adult
Failed Step: Change the infant's 'Assigned to' adult and re-check the exit-row seat's displayed state.
Notes: Same UI-defect finding as EXR-004: switching the infant's Assigned to between adults changed nothing about the seat's displayed state or availability.

Title: A return trip gives one seat map per journey
Notes: The ancillaries step rendered two of everything (meals, baggage, seat selection, included-baggage panels), each correctly labelled with its own journey.

Title: Seat maps are completely separate per journey
Notes: Onward and return seat maps are completely separate: the same seat number was simultaneously held on one leg and free on the other; assigning a seat on one leg left the other map's counter at 0.

Title: Three journeys give three seat maps and three sets of ancillaries
Failed Step: Open Ancillaries on a 2-leg multi-city booking and check for one Extra Baggage panel per journey.
Notes: Partly Passed, partly Failed on a 2-leg multi-city itinerary: seat maps and meal panels were correctly split one-per-flight, but the Extra Baggage panel existed only for the outbound leg and was entirely absent for the return leg - the same underlying journey-scoping defect as TC-SM-MCT-006.

Title: A seat booked on one flight never appears against another
Notes: Submitting Hold on the 2-leg multi-city itinerary failed with a browser-level CORS error on the fare-recheck-hold call, before the page ever navigated away from Passenger Info. The precondition (a completed Hold/Book to inspect) could not be reached at all - recorded Blocked by this technical error, not scored Pass/Fail. Raised separately as its own technical finding, not folded into the case verdict.

Title: Seat maps follow FLIGHTS, fare packages follow JOURNEYS
Notes: Needs one journey spanning multiple connecting flights; the only working multi-city route found this session (CAI-JED-CAI) is two independent single-flight journeys, not a connecting one, so this case remains untestable on this itinerary.

Title: Seats and ancillaries survive to the confirmation page per flight
Notes: Same CORS blocker as TC-SM-MCT-004 - the Hold needed to reach the confirmation/e-ticket page never completed. Not scored Pass/Fail.

Title: Extra baggage should say which flight it belongs to
Failed Step: Open Ancillaries on a 2-leg multi-city booking and check baggage options are journey-scoped.
Notes: On the 2-leg multi-city trip, only one Extra Baggage panel exists (headed for the outbound leg); the return leg's baggage options are not offered anywhere. Confirms the sheet's own known-fault class (baggage not correctly scoped per journey), though the exact shape (missing panel vs merged/mislabelled panel) differs from the sheet's original description.

Title: Seat and ancillary charges should be identifiable per journey
Failed Step: Select a paid seat on each leg of a 2-leg multi-city booking and inspect the Fare Breakdown.
Notes: Reproduces the sheet's own known fault exactly: with one seat on each of two separate flights, the Fare Breakdown showed one merged base-fare line, one merged tax line and one merged Seat Selection total (614+236=850) - none itemised per journey.

Title: The confirmation total equals what was quoted
Notes: Order Costing tab's fare total (8,987.80) plus SSR total (1,795.00) equalled the recorded Total Booking Amount (10,782.80), matching the quoted price at Hold/Pay exactly.

Title: Every price line survives the booking unchanged
Notes: Same evidence as CNF-001 - every price line (fare, meal, baggage, seat) survived to the order unchanged.

Title: Every ancillary reaches the confirmation with its own price
Notes: The order's Segment Ancillaries tab lists meal, baggage and seat separately, each with its own price, matching what was chosen.

Title: Seats carry through to the right passenger with the right price
Notes: The seat is listed under the correct passenger's own ancillary block, same seat number and same price as at booking.

Title: Infants appear as passengers but carry no seat or ancillaries
Notes: This particular order has no infant (1 adult only), so the counting behaviour could not be checked on it directly; already covered on the separate 4-passenger booking earlier in this run, where the infant correctly had zero ancillary sections (TC-SM-PAX-001).

Title: The e-ticket and the confirmation page agree exactly
Notes: PNR, ticket number, status and total all matched exactly between the confirmation-at-booking and the Order Details page read later.

Title: The wallet is reduced by exactly the booking amount
Notes: Verified via TC-PAH-002's wallet reconciliation: the wallet dropped by exactly the booking's recorded total (10,782.800 EGP), to the millieme, with no gap - this corroborates run-006's root-cause read that flynas's 1.22-1.64 EGP shortfall was a SAR/EGP conversion artifact, since Air Cairo prices natively in EGP with no conversion and shows none.

Title: The Costing tab adds up and is the figure to trust
Notes: The Costing tab's Total Sales Amount, Total Net Amount and Total Booking Amount all independently agreed at 10,782.80 EGP, matching the fare+SSR arithmetic exactly.

Title: The order page itemises every ancillary and reconciles
Notes: The order's Costing tab itemises Meal/Baggage/Seat as separate SSR components before rolling up to the booking total.

Title: Walking away before 'Book' creates nothing - THE SAFE TEST
Notes: A confirmed seat was navigated away from (to My Bookings) without pressing Book; the passenger's name appears in no booking afterward - walking away creates nothing.

Title: Extra baggage must not clash with the baggage already in the fare package
Notes: Air Cairo's baggage model has no discrete weight tiers (only per-kilogram/equipment items), so the exact same-weight clash this case requires cannot be constructed - already established under TC-BG-003. Not scored as a failure; flagged for test design to generalise the wording.

Title: A failed booking must be reported as failed everywhere
Notes: Checked all three named surfaces (confirmation/Order Details banner, Booking Details page, Dashboard) against a real failed order: all three correctly showed the failure (Booking Has been failed! / Booking Failed status / excluded from the Pending count) - none of the sheet's known-fault symptoms reproduced on this supplier.

Title: Going back a step must not silently throw away seats and ancillaries
Failed Step: From Ancillaries with a held seat, press Prev, edit the passenger's First Name, press Next.
Notes: Confirmed defect (cross-supplier, first found on flynas in run-006): editing a passenger's First Name after choosing ancillaries silently discarded the held seat and its EGP 1,180 fare line, with no warning, toast or dialog. High/P1 - see Defect Register.

Title: Two infant-holding adults cannot sit in the same set of seats
Notes: Final verdict after two confound-free retries: with an invalid-document confound removed, a real Book attempt with two infant-holding adults in the same 3-seat set was genuinely rejected (Invalid request); a fresh Hold attempt with fresh document numbers was rejected identically. The rule is enforced at order submission, just not in the seat-map UI (an earlier UI-only reading and a first Book attempt were confounded/inconclusive and are superseded by this result).

Title: Seat map and ancillary prices use the right exchange rate
Notes: Air Cairo prices natively in EGP with no currency conversion at any point, so there is no Rate-Of-Exchange division for this case to check. Not scored as a failure.

Title: Meals are offered per passenger and per flight
Notes: 3 Meal Preference sections appeared, one each for both adults and the child, each with its own journey heading; the infant had none.

Title: An infant is not offered a meal
Notes: The infant had no meal section at all (not empty or disabled) on a 4-passenger booking.

Title: Choosing and removing a meal changes the price correctly
Notes: Adding a meal added exactly its price as its own fare line; removing it returned the total to precisely the starting figure with no residue.

Title: The chosen meal reaches the confirmation (SPENDS REAL MONEY)
Notes: On a real completed booking, the chosen meal (code, name, price) matched exactly between the pre-booking fare breakdown, the confirmation/order page and the e-ticket.

Title: Extra baggage is offered per passenger and per journey
Notes: 3 Extra Baggage sections appeared, one each for both adults and the child, each with its own journey heading; the infant had none.

Title: An infant is not offered extra baggage
Notes: The infant had no baggage section at all on the same 4-passenger booking.

Title: Changing the bag weight replaces the bag, it does not add a second one
Notes: Exercised against the case's real intent (swapping one baggage selection for another, since this supplier sells items rather than weight tiers): changing the selection produced exactly one Extra Baggage line at the new price, not two stacked. Wording flagged for test design to generalise per supplier.

Title: The extra bag reaches the confirmation (SPENDS REAL MONEY)
Notes: On a real completed booking, the chosen extra bag (item and price) matched exactly between the pre-booking fare breakdown, the confirmation/order page and the e-ticket, alongside the separately-shown included baggage allowance.

Title: Seats, meals and bags chosen before holding are kept on the held booking
Notes: A real Hold booking (PNR 8ANO44) retained the seat, meal and extra baggage chosen before holding, with the fare reconciling exactly and the wallet unmoved (a Hold does not charge).

Title: Paying takes exactly the booking amount from the wallet
Notes: Paying the held booking debited the wallet by exactly the booking total (10,782.800 EGP), to the millieme.

Title: A price change between hold and payment is shown before paying
Notes: Reopening the held booking before paying showed the same Net Payable amount as at Hold - no price had changed, so the if-unchanged-the-held-price-is-charged branch applied and no change dialog was due.

Title: After payment the e-ticket is issued and matches the booking
Notes: After payment the booking moved Hold -> Confirmed, a ticket number was issued, and every e-ticket field (passenger, flight, meal, seat, baggage) matched what was held.

Title: A supplier with no fare packages shows no package step
Notes: With Bundle correctly Not Supported, the wizard shows no fare-package step or Fare Bundles & Services section at all, and the Included Baggage panel shows concrete fixed-to-fare values instead of depends on bundle.

Title: The same flight gives a different map in each cabin
Notes: Air Cairo has no Business cabin on this route: a Business search returned the same five Economy fares, each explicitly labelled No Business. This is a route/environment limitation, not a failure - there is no second cabin's map to compare against.

Title: 'Not offered' sections can be told apart from single taken seats
Notes: Same reason as TC-SM-CAB-001 - no second (Business) cabin map exists on this route to compare Not offered sections against.

Title: The Business row has its middle seats blocked
Notes: Same reason as TC-SM-CAB-001 - no Business row exists on this route to check for a blocked-middle-seat pattern.

Title: A two-cabin aircraft shows both cabins properly
Notes: Same reason as TC-SM-CAB-001 - no second cabin exists on this route/supplier combination to render at all.
